To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the subsidies to PV in Japan through the buy back program are cost effective for reducing CO2 emission.

(i) the cost effectiveness of the subsidies to photovoltaic in Japan from the view point of reducing CO2 emissions is about 33,000 JPY/t-CO2 in around 2025, (ii) the subsidies to photovolaic are necessary to make PV competitive with other energy technology even if both the fuel savings and green credits are taken into account, (iii) the annual revenue of the carbon tax is enough to finance the estimated annual subsidy.
subsidies to photovoltaic systems are not cost effective from a carbon emission reduction point of view.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cost effectiveness of subsidization to PV in Japan through an energy system analysis from CO2 reduction point of view.
the cost effectiveness of subsidizing photovoltaics (solar cells) in Japan.

the following questions: What would be the cost effectiveness of the buy back subsidy for photovoltaics (hereafter referred to as PV) in Japan? How would the cost effectiveness change as the carbon tax rate changes? How would it change as the PV system sales price changes? How would the buy back rate change as the PV capacity target changes?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subsidy to PV in Japan is cost effective from the point of view of reducing CO2 emissions.
the cost effectiveness of subsidy for PV in Japan is very high and it is a promising option for CO2 emission reduction.
the cost effectiveness of the PV subsidy is very high, but it is still not sufficient to justify the subsidy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cost effectiveness of PV subsidy from reducing CO2 emissions point of view is high enough for the Japanese government to consider PV as a promising technology for the future.
, if the CO2 emission reduction is taken into account, the cost effectiveness of PV subsidy in Japan is not as bad as it seems.
, if we want to achieve a significant reduction in CO2 emission, we have to take the cost effectiveness of the subsidies into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even if the carbon tax is introduced, PV system sales prices and electricity buy back prices need to be maintained at a high level in the near future.
the carbon tax alone will not be enough to promote PV.

the carbon tax is a very important tool in the fight against global warming and that it is necessary to establish a mechanism to collect the carbon tax revenue in order to use it for financing the subsidies.
